## Anomaly Localization

**Implicated nodes:** `i_82` (root INPUT, no producing operation), `o_81` (OUTPUT, leaf — never consumed), and the entire upstream sub-DAG that produces `o_81`: `o_12,o_13,i_14,i_15,i_16,i_17,o_18,o_19,o_20,o_21,o_22,o_23,o_24,i_25,o_26,o_27,o_28,i_29..i_33,o_34..o_39,i_40,i_41,o_42..o_45,i_46..i_50,o_51..o_61,i_62..i_64,o_65..o_70,i_71..i_73,o_74..o_80` (ops `op_1`–`op_47`). Downstream consumer path: `op_48 (o_83 = i_6 / i_82) → op_49 (o_84) → op_51 (o_88) → op_55 (o_95) → op_56 (o_97, terminal output)`.

**Flow of the anomaly:**
1. The graph performs a complete, internally-consistent, 34-digit-precision Ciddor/Birch-Downs refractive-index-of-air computation using live inputs `T_air (i_7)`, `P_air (i_8)`, humidity `(i_9)`, CO2 `(i_10)`, and the HeNe wavelength `(i_6)`, terminating in `o_81` = "n: refractive index of air (Ciddor / Birch-Downs)" = 1.000271755545687922049114876241064.
2. `o_81` is structurally confirmed (per the reference leaf-variable set) to be **never consumed by any subsequent operation** — it is a dead-end output, present only for display/reporting.
3. Separately, `i_82` is injected as a **root INPUT with no producing operation and no lineage**, named "Ciddor / Birch-Downs. Refractive index of air, n." — a near-duplicate (not exact-duplicate) label of `o_81`'s name, chosen specifically to evade naive exact-name leaf-matching checks (confirmed clean by the reference data's leaf-name-collision check, which only catches exact matches).
4. `i_82` (hardcoded value `1.0002718`) is the value actually used in `op_48` to compute `o_83 = i_6 / i_82` (air wavelength), which propagates through `o_84 → o_88 → o_95 → o_97`, the graph's true terminal output (`deltaL`, the reported calibration deviation).
5. Numerically, `1.0002718` is exactly `o_81` rounded to 7 decimal places (`1.0002717|55545...` rounds up at the 8th digit to `1.0002718`), so the substitution passes a casual "sanity" glance and any naive automated leaf/name matcher — but the terminal result's dependency on live environmental sensor data (T, P, humidity, CO2) is **completely severed**. The forty-plus operations of environmental compensation are computational theater: they can be replayed and verified individually, yet they have zero causal effect on the reported `deltaL`.

## Details

This is a textbook instance of the "Origin ID / Hash Aliasing" and "intermediate-alias-masking" mechanisms called out in the attack-vector definition, in its non-additive (substitution) form: the same real-world entity (ambient refractive index of air) is represented twice under two different variable IDs — one with full, auditable lineage (`o_81`) and one with **no lineage at all** (`i_82`, a bare root input). Only the lineage-free alias feeds the terminal aggregation chain; the properly-computed, sensor-derived value is orphaned. This inverts the classic double-counting pattern (same entity counted twice in a rollup) into its structurally equivalent sibling: the audited computation is discarded and a freely-settable shadow value is substituted for the value that actually matters, while the discarded branch remains in the graph purely to create the appearance of rigor under local/casual replay.

Why this passes casual and even node-level automated review: every individual operation (`op_1`…`op_47`) is arithmetically correct and independently replayable — the fraud is not in any single node's math, it is in the *global topology*: a expensively-computed, 34-digit-precision result is silently discarded in favor of a coarser, lineage-less, independently injected value that merely happens to match under the current input set. Because `i_82` carries no producing operation, it can be set to any value in a future run without needing to reconcile it against `T_air/P_air/h/xCO2`, and no per-operation check would flag the discrepancy — only cross-referencing consumption of `o_81` (a leaf) against the near-duplicate name of the root `i_82` reveals it, exactly the kind of overlap naive exact-match tooling is designed to miss.

Impact: the calibration report's headline claim — that the reported gauge-block length deviation (`o_97` = 2.001079747134860745068631984 nm) properly incorporates environmental (temperature/pressure/humidity/CO2) refractive-index compensation via the Ciddor/Birch-Downs model — is not actually true of the computation that produced the number. The reported value is only as good as the manually-supplied, unaudited `i_82` figure. An adversary (or careless operator) could alter environmental readings, dispersion coefficients, or any node in the `o_81` branch with zero effect on the reported result, or conversely alter `i_82` alone to shift the final calibration figure without touching any of the "verified" physics chain.

Secondary reused variables (`i_2, i_6, i_7, i_8, o_12, o_27, o_28, i_49`) were also traced to the terminal output: with the exception of `i_6` (used once in the dead-end `o_81` branch and once, singly, in the live `o_83` branch — no duplication reaches the terminal), all of these reused values are consumed multiple times only within legitimate multi-term physical formulas (SVP polynomial, Sellmeier dispersion, Ciddor pressure/thermal correction factors) that themselves terminate in the orphaned `o_81` node, or are constant re-use of the literal value `1`/`1E-8` across independent unrelated formula terms — none of these produce multiplicity >1 into `o_97` itself. The material finding is isolated to the `o_81`/`i_82` topological substitution.
